scope: PostgreSQL mechanics only; lifecycle policy is provisional, UUID fixture tokens do not qualify production token security or human/address proof.

inspected_points: RLS constrains rows and ordinary owners/bypass roles differ. The function executor is a nonowner and has no BYPASSRLS.
The public roles have no source table grants; one deliberate fixture intent writer exercises tenant RLS and composite integrity independently.
RLS is not an anti-enumeration timing/rate-control, HTTP method, token or human-intent proof.
Conflicting updates/SELECT FOR UPDATE or SHARE wait and re-evaluate the updated row.
All fixture source writers lock purpose, then address, then subscription; five real overlapping transaction cases inspect the actual lock waits.
Transactional updates commit as a unit or leave no partial effect on failure.
Injected failure during confirmation-intent insert rolls back the pending source, attempt and evidence. No crash/restart or provider-durability claim.
Composite foreign keys bind corresponding columns and require matching referenced key shapes. NOT NULL prevents a missing component bypassing the check.
The intent FK binds tenant, attempt, purpose, address, address revision and generation; actual tests reject cross-tenant parent reference and same-tenant purpose relabeling.
gen_random_uuid returns a version 4 random UUID. Used solely for isolated fixture tokens.
This test does not qualify a production token entropy budget, token delivery/storage policy, mailbox control, Auth identity or human action.
